title: Reported Speech — Questions & Commands
subtitle: Report what someone asked or told someone to do, not just what they said.
objectives: Report wh- questions, keeping the question word
Report commands and requests with "tell/ask + object + infinitive"

content.intro: You already know how to report statements. Real conversations also include questions and commands — reporting those needs a different structure, not just the same backshift rule.

rules.heading: a) Reporting yes/no questions
rules.body:
Use if or whether, and switch back to normal statement word order (no auxiliary inversion).

  • "Do you like coffee?" → She asked if I liked coffee.
  • "Are you coming?" → He asked whether I was coming.

rules.heading: b) Reporting wh- questions
rules.body:
Keep the question word, but use normal statement word order.

  • "Where do you live?" → She asked where I lived.
  • "What time is it?" → He asked what time it was.

rules.heading: c) Reporting commands and requests
rules.body:
tell/ask + object + (not) + to-infinitive — no backshifting needed, since the infinitive doesn't change.

  • "Close the door." → She told me to close the door.
  • "Please don't be late." → He asked me not to be late.

examples: She asked if I liked coffee.
He asked whether I was coming.
He asked what time it was.
She told me to close the door.
He asked me not to be late.

commonMistakes.wrong: She asked did I like coffee.
commonMistakes.right: She asked if I liked coffee.
commonMistakes.why: Reported yes/no questions need "if/whether" and normal word order, not the original question form.

commonMistakes.wrong: He asked where did I live.
commonMistakes.why: Reported wh- questions keep the question word but drop the auxiliary inversion.

commonMistakes.wrong: She told me close the door.
commonMistakes.right: She told me to close the door.
commonMistakes.why: Reported commands need "to" before the infinitive.

commonMistakes.wrong: He asked me to not be late.
commonMistakes.right: He asked me not to be late.
commonMistakes.why: The negative goes before "to," not between "to" and the verb.

items.prompt: "Do you have a car?" → She asked ___ I had a car.
"Where do you work?" → He asked ___ I ___.
items.explanation: Reported wh- question — keep the question word, normal word order.

items.prompt: "Open the window." → She told me ___ the window.
"Please don't shout." → He asked me ___ shout.
"What time does the train leave?" → She asked ___
options: what time did the train leave
what time does the train leave
items.explanation: Reported wh- question: keep the question word, use normal statement word order.

items.prompt: "Can you help me?" → He asked ___ help him.
items.explanation: Reported yes/no question: if + subject + backshifted modal (could).

items.incorrect: She asked where was I going.
answer: She asked where I was going.
items.explanation: Reported wh- questions use normal statement word order, not question order.

items.incorrect: He told me open the door.
answer: He told me to open the door.
items.explanation: Reported commands need "to" before the infinitive.

summary: Yes/no questions → if/whether + normal word order.
Wh- questions → keep the question word + normal word order.
